blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Coordinating inbound and outbound flows means treating them as one rhythm, not two separate queues. Good teams stagger their docks: inbound arrivals in the morning, outbound departures in the afternoon, with a clear window in between for picking and packing. That simple shape reduces congestion, so trucks do not queue outside and pallets do not sit blocking aisles.

Communication matters as much as the schedule. If inbound is running late, outbound needs to know early, so they can re-plan instead of reacting in panic. If outbound is flexing a lot, inbound can prioritise the items that go out first.

Although the work is different, the goal is the same: keep the whole building moving without anyone tripping over anyone else.

items.q: According to the text, how should inbound and outbound flows be treated?
items.why: "treating them as one rhythm, not two separate queues."

items.q: How do good teams stagger their docks?
options: Inbound in the morning, outbound in the afternoon
Both flows at the same time
Outbound in the morning, inbound in the afternoon
Inbound and outbound only at night
items.why: "inbound arrivals in the morning, outbound departures in the afternoon."

items.q: According to the text, what happens when inbound is running late?
options: Outbound needs to know early so it can re-plan
The docks are closed for the day
items.why: "If inbound is running late, outbound needs to know early, so they can re-plan instead of reacting in panic."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Early communication of delays is valuable
Inbound and outbound should be managed in complete isolation
A clear window between flows helps picking and packing
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende coordenar os dois fluxos como um só ritmo, não isolá-los.

items.q: What does "without anyone tripping over anyone else" suggest?
options: Staff should work in separate buildings
Only one flow can operate at a time
The flows should physically block each other for safety
Well-coordinated flows avoid getting in each other's way
items.why: Inferência: é uma imagem para dizer que os fluxos coexistem sem atrapalhar um ao outro.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver explicando o novo cronograma das docas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, thanks for coming down to the yard. Let me walk you through why the schedule has to change. For the last three weeks, inbound trucks have been queueing outside because the docks were still full of outbound pallets waiting for packing space. Nothing was moving, and everyone was tripping over everyone else.

So here is the new shape. From Monday, inbound books in before eleven, outbound departs after one, and we keep the midday hour as a buffer slot. That gap absorbs a late arrival without pushing the whole afternoon back.

Now, this only works if we talk to each other. If a supplier tells us their truck is delayed, I want outbound to hear it straight away, not at four o'clock when the aisles are already jammed. Early warning means we re-plan calmly instead of firefighting.

Although inbound and outbound feel like two different jobs, from the yard's point of view it is one rhythm. If we get the timing right, the trucks stop queueing, the pallets stop blocking the aisles, and nobody stands around waiting.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why were inbound trucks queueing outside for the last three weeks?
options: The docks were full of outbound pallets waiting for packing
The suppliers were arriving too early
The yard had been closed for repairs
items.why: "inbound trucks have been queueing outside because the docks were still full of outbound pallets waiting for packing space."

items.q: What is the purpose of the midday buffer slot?
options: To give staff a longer lunch break
To let outbound depart before inbound arrives
To absorb a late arrival without pushing the afternoon back
To close the docks for cleaning
items.why: "we keep the midday hour as a buffer slot. That gap absorbs a late arrival without pushing the whole afternoon back."

items.q: When does Oliver want outbound to hear about a delayed truck?
options: Only once the truck has arrived
At four o'clock when the aisles are jammed
At the end of the week
items.why: "I want outbound to hear it straight away, not at four o'clock when the aisles are already jammed."

items.q: What does Oliver imply the new schedule depends on to succeed?
options: People communicating with each other in time
items.why: Inferência: "this only works if we talk to each other" — a coordenação depende da comunicação.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's attitude in this talk?
options: Uncertain about whether change is needed
Practical and focused on fixing the flow
items.why: Inferência: ele explica a causa e apresenta uma solução concreta e calma, sem culpar ninguém.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Good teams stagger their docks across the day." To stagger here means to…
items.why: To stagger = escalonar, distribuir em horários diferentes.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When both flows hit the docks at once, ___ builds up and trucks queue outside."
items.why: Congestion = congestionamento, o acúmulo que trava a doca.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If outbound is ___ a lot, inbound can prioritise the items that go out first."
items.why: To flex = variar, oscilar na demanda ou no volume.

items.q: "Pallets were left blocking the aisles." An aisle is…
options: a passage between rows or shelves
items.why: Aisle = corredor, o espaço de passagem entre fileiras.

items.q: "When inbound runs late, outbound has to re-plan." To re-plan means to…
options: make a new plan to adapt
items.why: To re-plan = replanejar, refazer o plano para se adaptar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de operação e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The supervisor still has to sign off on the new dock schedule." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the staggered docks warehouse by warehouse." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "When outbound is behind, inbound should flag up the delay early." To flag up means to…
options: raise or point out the issue
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para um problema cedo.

items.q: "Two team leads pushed back on the afternoon-only outbound rule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "A tidier chart alone will not move the needle on congestion." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
